subject: Runtime paths: hosted access checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@gridpay.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime paths: hosted access checklist & next steps

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap from my side and a short list of asks so we can map the right deployment pathway (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). I want to keep this tight so your engineers can decide which runway makes sense for the pilot.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Use case: real-time payment confirmation and user-facing transaction summaries (low single-digit seconds SLA).
- Peak traffic: spikes during payroll runs; expect short daily bursts up to ~120 QPS for inference.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts but customer-authorized; compliance review ongoing (SOC2).

Deployment considerations (what we recommend initially):
- Hosted API: fast to onboard, sandbox endpoints available, good for first 2–3 week pilot. Prefix/KV caching and short batching reduce token cost for repeated transaction templates.
- Dedicated: recommended if you need reserved GPUs for sustained high concurrency or strict latency SLOs during payroll windows.
- Private VPC/on-prem: appropriate if regulatory requirements mandate customer-controlled networking or HSM for keys.

Asks / next steps from GridPay engineering to confirm pilot path:
1) Share a 48h traffic sample or the attached traffic_profile.xlsx (already uploaded to the Drive link). This helps us size endpoints and suggest rate slices.
2) Confirm whether prompts will include full customer PII or just a tokenized reference (PII in prompts pushes us toward Private VPC or additional processing).
3) Decide desired pilot duration and whether you want a single endpoint (simpler) or separate read/write endpoints for inference vs. post-processing.

What Redwood will provide once we get the traffic sample:
- A recommended quickstart plan (endpoints, rate caps, caching profile) — see attached redwood_hosted_quickstart.pdf (stub).
- Sandbox credentials and a short checklist (network egress, CORS, API key install).
- Guidance on transition triggers from Hosted -> Dedicated (concurrency thresholds, sustained tokens/day).

Proposed timeline:
- You share traffic_profile.xlsx by Thu 21 May.
- We return a Hosted quickstart plan by Mon 25 May.
- Kickoff sandbox testing the week of Mon 1 Jun.

If Hosted looks like a clean fit for the pilot, we can provision sandbox endpoints today and scope burst/dedicated options in parallel. If procurement wants to evaluate Dedicated or Private, we can introduce the Dedicated sizing worksheet and our security package for VPCs.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with sandbox access as soon as you confirm the traffic sample availability.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_hosted_quickstart.pdf - PDF)
(Attachment: gridpay_traffic_profile.xlsx - XLSX)

Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Runtime paths: hosted access checklist & next steps

Diego — thanks for the clear summary. Quick answers from our side: we can share an anonymized 72h token-level sample by Wednesday EOD (will send the Drive link). For privacy, prompts will include hashed customer IDs and last4 card digits, but not SSNs; we likely need audit logs for the pilot.

A few clarifying Qs before the sandbox: 
- For Hosted, can you confirm the per-second rate cap we should expect in the sandbox and whether we can request a short burst increase for payroll tests?
- If we start in Hosted and need Dedicated later, roughly what lead time do you need to reserve capacity and what minimum commit sizes are typical?

Procurement looped in: procurement@gridpay.io — they want a short checklist of security artifacts for review (SOC2, data retention, encryption at rest).

Happy to get you the sample Wednesday.

—Sarah
Director of Product, GridPay

Great — thanks Sarah, appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers and concrete next actions below.

Answers:
- Sandbox rate caps: default sandbox endpoint set to 50 RPS and 300 concurrent tokens/sec for initial access. We can grant a one-off 4hr burst to 150 RPS for your payroll test upon request (please give a target date and a 24h notice).
- Dedicated lead time & commits: typical lead time for reserved Dedicated pools is 10–14 business days after SOW sign; entry-level monthly commit starts around the mid-five-figure range depending on model footprint. I’ll loop in our Sales Ops if you want ballpark pricing today.
- Security artifacts: attaching the SOC2 summary + public encryption-at-rest overview; Monica from our security team can run through any deeper requests.

Immediate next steps we’ll take once you drop the anonymized sample:
1) We’ll size a Hosted sandbox endpoint and return a short config (endpoint URL, per-route rate caps, cache TTLs) within 48 hours.
2) We’ll include the exact trigger thresholds we recommend for switching to Dedicated (sustained 24h average concurrency and tokens/day numbers).
3) Provide a one-page procurement checklist for SOC2, retention, and KMS options.

Action items for GridPay:
- Sarah / engineering: upload anonymized token sample to the Drive link by Wed EOD (confirmed).
- Procurement: send any contract redline expectations so we can surface to Sales Ops.

I’ll also attach a short runbook for sandbox onboarding in a follow-up. If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute ops preflight with your infra lead and Monica to validate egress, IP allowlisting, and KMS options.

Thanks — looking forward to the sample.

Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
